key_insight: Most surveyed patients and carers supported AI-based duodenal biopsy diagnosis, while stakeholders emphasised accuracy evidence, human oversight and transparency.
clinical_relevance: AI could help address pathology workload and diagnostic delays, but this study assessed stakeholder views rather than diagnostic performance or patient outcomes.
method: Mixed-methods engagement using questionnaires, workshops and thematic analysis.
Patient/carer survey: 231 respondents; four UK focus-group workshops.
Healthcare professional survey: 37 respondents; education-session attitudes assessed in 34 matched pairs.
evidence_signal: Patient/carer support was 68.4%; in the 34 matched pairs, agreement on trust rose from 38.2% before education to 67.6% afterward.
watch_item: Small professional and pre/post samples limit generalisability; clinical adoption still requires validation, governance and workflow integration.
paper_title: Patient, carer and clinical stakeholder views on using artificial intelligence and machine learning for the histopathological diagnosis of duodenal biopsies
